# Google Display Network vs. Programmatic Display Ads: What’s the Right Choice?

By 

Samantha Record, Partnership Development Manager

•

2

Minute Read

Video

•

June 27, 2025

July 1, 2026

Google Display Advertising might seem like a simple choice, but the platform has it's short-comings. Let's compare how it stacks up against a Programmatic Advertising strategy.

When it comes to digital advertising, understanding the difference between Google Display Network and [Programmatic Display Ads](https://www.awarity.com/banner-ads) is key to making the right choice for your needs. Google Display Network offers a user-friendly platform for ad placements through Google's network. **However, its straightforward approach can limit targeting precision and campaign customization.**

Programmatic Advertising offers the ability to increase precision by leveraging advanced algorithms and A.I. to deliver hyper-targeted ads across a broader range of platforms. This ensures cost efficiency without sacrificing reach, allowing businesses to maximize their precision targeting and real-time adjustments.

**Some of the key differences between Google Display Network and Programmatic Advertising to consider when choosing your platform include:**

**1. Reach** – Google Display Network is limited to Google’s ecosystem, whereas Programmatic Advertising can access broader inventory across multiple ad exchanges leading to a wider audience. Programmatic advertising can access a much wider assortment of placements than Google Display Network, achieving higher quality placements on numerous sites and apps.

**2\. Targeting** – Google Display Network’s targeting mainly utilizes interests and keyword-based tactics, while Programmatic Advertising can include behavioral and contextual targeting that identifies a broader audience.

**3\. Cost and Efficiency** – Google Display Network can be simple to setup but without more advanced optimization tools, campaigns can deliver wasted impressions to the wrong audience, leading to higher costs. At Awarity, our Programmatic Advertising campaigns are managed with real-time A.I. optimization, ensuring each impression counts for greater efficiency. With tools like this, Programmatic Display can achieve far greater results by reaching the right audience consistently, at a lower cost than Google Display.

While some marketers lean on Google Display Network for its simplicity, choosing Programmatic Advertising ensures greater results with campaigns that are highly targeted and optimized for greater reach. # GDN vs. Programmatic: How to Combine Both for a Winning Media Mix

GDN vs. programmatic advertising: What's the real difference? Learn how automation can help you balance Google's network with the open web to maximize digital ad spend.

_What is the difference between_ [_programmatic advertising and the Google Display Network_](https://www.fluency.inc/videos/advertising-leader-perspectives-programmatic-google-display-with-andy-macleay)_? GDN provides access to Google-owned and partnered inventory, while programmatic advertising uses demand-side platforms to access a much wider array of ad exchanges and premium placements across the open web. Relying exclusively on the Google Display Network limits your agency's ability to reach audiences across the wider internet. While GDN offers tried-and-true reliability, combining it with broader_ [_programmatic advertising through a demand-side platform_](https://www.fluency.inc/blog/programmatic-execution-at-scale-key-considerations-for-2025) _gives your team access to expanded ad inventory and_ [_advanced audience targeting capabilities._](https://www.fluency.inc/blog/ad-strategist-playbook-how-to-activate-local-audience-data-at-scale) _This guide explains how to_ [_build a media mix that leverages both Google's network and programmatic channels_](https://www.fluency.inc/videos/advertising-leader-perspectives-programmatic-google-display-with-andy-macleay) _to maximize digital advertising spend._

\---

Global digital advertising spend continues to show no signs of slowing down. Global ad spend is [expected to rise 4.6% in 2024](https://www.dentsu.com/news-releases/dentsu-forecasts-2024-global-ad-spend-to-grow), bringing the total to $752.8 billion. At the same time, the digital advertising industry as a whole is projected to increase by 6.5% this year—-reaching $442.6 billion and accounting for 58.8% of total spend.

Traditionally, many advertisers have relied on the Google Display Network (GDN) for [programmatic media](https://www.fluency.inc/blog/programmatic-execution-at-scale-key-considerations-for-2024). This approach limits your ability to access the wider ad inventory that lives outside of Google. 

Now, with expanded ad inventory and diverse programmatic media from [DSPs like Basis Technologies](https://www.fluency.inc/video-library/advertising-leader-perspectives-programmatic-automation-with-basis-with-andy-macleay), advertisers must combine Google and programmatic for an effective media mix.

Programmatic and traditional display advertising both offer sophisticated ways to connect with potential consumers. But many advertisers are overwhelmed by the growing complexity of available platforms. 

In this article, we’ll clarify: 

*   the [benefits of programmatic advertising](https://www.fluency.inc//blog/2024-guide-to-programmatic-advertising-benefits-trends-and-challenges) and traditional display advertising on Google
*   the differences between emerging programmatic advertising and traditional display advertising on Google
*   reasons to consider programmatic or traditional display advertising 
*   how to strategically invest your time and resources into these different platforms based on your overall goals

## Is the Google Display Network considered programmatic advertising?

Yes, the Google Display Network (GDN) is technically a basic form of programmatic advertising because it uses automation to buy and place ads. However, it operates as a "walled garden" limited to Google's ecosystem. True programmatic advertising utilizes independent Demand-Side Platforms (DSPs) to bid on inventory across the entire open web, far beyond what Google controls.

## What are the benefits of the Google Display Network (GDN)?

The Google Display Network (GDN) allows advertisers to reach their audience via mobile apps, YouTube, email, etc. This multi-channel approach ensures a broad visibility for brands. GDN also increases the chances of engagement, as users are exposed to ads in different contexts throughout their day. 

Some key benefits of GDN include: 

*   **Improved overall campaign effectiveness.** The right message reaches the right people at the right time.
*   **Boosted brand recognition and recall.** Repetitive exposure to visual content reinforces brand identity. 
*   **Engaging and memorable ads.** The versatility of GDN ad formats—ranging from banners to video ads—allows for creative storytelling opportunities.

## What are the benefits of programmatic advertising?

Programmatic advertising offers a number of advanced capabilities that make it a preferred choice over relying solely on GDN.

For example, programmatic advertising includes [advanced audience targeting](https://www.fluency.inc/blog/ad-strategist-playbook-how-to-activate-local-audience-data-at-scale) and diverse ad placement options. Programmatic advertising excels in reach, ad variety, and deal-making options. 

On the flip side, programmatic advertising may involve higher costs compared to GDN, which typically requires smaller budgets and offers multiple payment models. 

Organizations can leverage programmatic advertising to:

*   **Enhance their online presence.** Brands can optimize their website and content for search engines and strategically utilize social media. For example, implementing interactive content like polls, quizzes, and videos fosters a deeper connection with users. 
*   **Drive conversions in an increasingly competitive market**. Organizations can track user interactions and continuously refining marketing strategies to effectively guide potential customers through the buying journey. This can increase both conversion rates and sales.
